title: Smile For Me: Putunia and Jerafina response comparisons

people.name: Yugo Limbo
people.role: Co-creator (official press credits); animator, game developer and comic artist (official studio biography)

people.name: Day Lane
people.role: Co-creator (official press credits); producer, programmer and gameplay designer (official studio biography)

summary: Official side-by-side nod/shake GIFs connect expression references directly to a player's conversational response.

observations.text: The sampled Putunia frame pairs a small, clenched-looking mouth and intense narrow eyes with a raised boxing glove and question marks. The body and face both support the confrontational line.
The sampled Jerafina frame uses a tilted face, conspicuous lips, a relaxed seated pose and crossed legs for a very different conversational attitude from Putunia.

The official page supplies comparison GIFs named for nod/shake responses. The press history attributes the nod-and-shake controls to Day and the collage-art and live-action puppetry direction to Yugo.

mistIdeas: Our inference: design separate acknowledging and declining responses. A nod should settle into attentive eyes, while a decline could use a small sideways gaze and a restrained mouth instead of a universal happy bounce.
Our inference: retain a little character attitude during interaction. The same input can have more personality than a generic checkmark.

title: In Stars and Time: Odile's wry reassurance
studio: insertdisc5; published by Armor Games Studios

people.name: Adrienne Bazir (insertdisc5)
people.role: Game developer and cartoonist with 2D animation experience; developer of In Stars and Time. Individual portrait animation credit not established here.

summary: A half-smile and tired, pinched eyes make reassurance sound dry and complicated before the sentence is finished.

observations.text: In the official Odile screenshot, the mouth lifts in a small uneven smile while the eyes remain heavily lidded. The inner brow area pinches upward. The combination reads as wry concern rather than uncomplicated happiness; that emotional reading is our visual interpretation.
The portrait reaches above the dialogue box and includes an angled upper body. This lets the face retain its fine eye and mouth shapes while the torso supplies a relaxed attitude.

The official battle screenshot gives four simultaneous face treatments: a narrow-eyed smirk, a worried mouth with sweat, an active open-mouth attack pose, and a downturned tired face. Their differences remain readable without hue.

mistIdeas: Our inference: author a reassuring-but-unsure pose with a small smile, lowered lids and a slight inward lift at the brow; avoid moving every feature toward a single happy/sad label.

Our inference: use a three-pose cue sequence for a difficult answer: attentive hold, wry acknowledgement at the qualifying clause, then a quieter recovery. Exact durations would need testing; none are measured from this screenshot.

Our inference: judge the expression in grayscale and at final display size before adding color or effects. Preserve MIST's silhouette while changing the relationship between lid angle and mouth asymmetry.

title: Chicory: Alexis Dean-Jones's feeling-first character poses

people.name: Alexis Dean-Jones
people.role: Artist & Animator; character design and animation

summary: The animator's published development drawings show how head angle, eyelids and mouth silhouette can carry a feeling before motion is added.

observations.text: The published dog sketchbook page includes a huge open-mouth, raised-brush pose alongside compressed, side-looking and smaller-mouth poses. Eye size, mouth opening and head angle change together.
The adjacent character study contrasts drooping lids and lowered heads with sharply angled profiles. These are pose drawings, not evidence of transition timing.
Dean-Jones says she often starts with a feeling and conveys it through expression or pose, and uses animal videos to understand movement, angles and proportions.

mistIdeas: Our inference: draw one unmistakable still for listening, uncertainty, recognition and delight before animating any transition.
Our inference: coordinate MIST's eye aperture and mouth opening around the same feeling; avoid mixing a delighted mouth with an unrelated neutral gaze.
Our inference: make acknowledgement a change in head/face orientation plus expression, then hold long enough to read before recovering.

title: UNDERTALE: Flowey's polite face and emotional denial

people.name: Toby Fox
people.role: UNDERTALE creator and interviewer; exact authorship of the selected Alarm Clock portrait pixels is not established by the page.

people.name: Temmie Chang
people.role: UNDERTALE art collaborator; separately credited as Main Artist and Main Animator on DELTARUNE Chapter 2. This is not an attribution of the Flowey portraits to her.

summary: An official sequence pairs simple smiling portraits with denial, embarrassment and a remembered act of care, giving useful examples of a face saying more than its words.

observations.text: The bicycle sequence changes the eye and mouth treatment while preserving Flowey's flower outline, stem and overall placement. A narrowed-eyed expression accompanies his hypothetical gift; later the face returns to a plain open-eyed smile when the desired bicycle is specified.

In the inspected panels, a large-eyed smile accompanies the claim that a gift would waste everyone's time. This mismatch between friendly mouth and defensive language is a useful mixed-affect reading, not a claim about a documented production method.

The published panel order includes standalone pauses before and after a painful memory. These are readable dialogue beats on a static page; the page does not establish how many milliseconds the game would hold them.
In Toby Fox's interview, Temmie recalls being impressed by Flowey's acting and laugh in an early demo. This is evidence of the creators' attention to acting, not proof that Temmie animated the scene.

mistIdeas: Our inference: keep the body or chassis nearly fixed during a spoken thought, then change the face when the intention changes. This gives a small eye or mouth change more weight.

Our inference: for an awkward admission, hold a socially pleasant mouth while the eyes narrow or avert, insert a still pause, then let the mouth soften. This should be authored as an acting cue, not a generic idle loop.
Our inference: separate speech-mouth motion from the expressive mouth pose so the expression can remain readable during silence. Use the phrase boundary and the emotional turn as cue inputs.

title: Great God Grove: contrasting god faces

people.name: Yugo Limbo
people.role: Developer (with Day Lane); animator in official studio biography

summary: A supplied god-dialogue GIF juxtaposes very different face designs while keeping the speaking face large and readable.

observations.text: One sampled frame pairs a long green face with closed angled eyelids on the left and a round orange face with star-shaped eyes and a small pinched mouth on the right. The compact mouth marks contrast with very different eye silhouettes.
The official press kit specifically credits Jack Cornish for 3d animations; it credits Day Lane and Yugo Limbo as developers.

mistIdeas: Our inference: test emotional eye silhouettes independently from mouth size. Small closed or pinched mouths can carry a feeling when the lids or pupils already establish it.
Our inference: include at least one inward-looking pose with closed angled lids. Keep it visually different from an ordinary blink.

media.alt: Side-by-side god dialogue with contrasting eye and mouth designs
